alignments.note: Waw rendered *also*, which English writes postpositively; the unit is discontinuous rather than broken (rule 51).
Preposition to *for*.
`לֶחֶם הַמַּעֲרֶכֶת` carried by the single English word *showbread*; both lexemes stand inside it, so the head goes to the governing morpheme, the construct (rules 23, 30).
The separately segmented article takes the written *the* beside the fused expression, exactly as in `דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים` → *the chronicles* (rule 30).
Waw to *and*.
Preposition to *for*.

One substantive rendered by a multi-word phrase with a supplied determiner; head on the word carrying the lexeme, since *flour* alone is any flour (rules 15, 31). The competing reading heads on *flour* as a class noun, named under rule 8.
Preposition to *for*.
One substantive rendered by a multi-word phrase, headed on the word carrying the lexeme as `עֹלָה` → *burnt offerings* is (rule 31); the indefinite article is the noun's own under rule 15.
The Hebrew writes a connective of its own for each member, so no correlative pair is to be placed and each waw takes only the English word written for it: this one takes *whether* (rule 14).
Preposition to *of*.
Construct noun; the chain is rendered attributively under rule 28.
The ASV writes no *the* for this phrase at all, so the article is unrendered (rule 29).
Rectum rendered attributively (rule 28).
Waw rendered *or*.
Preposition to *of*.
Assimilated article morpheme on the noun `מַחֲבַת` takes the *the* standing before that noun's own word (rules 12, 29).

One Hebrew nominal recast as an English head noun plus relative clause; the supplied antecedent, relative and verb join the noun's own unit and the head goes on *pan*, which carries the noun's own lexeme (rule 46). Discontinuous around the article's *the* (rule 25).
Waw rendered *or*.
Preposition to *of*.

The substantival article on the participle takes the pronoun the ASV supplies to make it substantival, headed on that pronoun rather than on the relative that follows it, exactly as `הָרַע` → *that which was evil* is read (rule 41). An article morpheme is present here, so rule 46's anarthrous case does not govern.
The participle keeps its own English together with the copula the ASV supplies, which stays with it under rule 20; head on the word carrying the lexeme (rule 41).
Waw to *and*.
Preposition to *for*.
The quantifier takes the generic *manner* the ASV supplies to expand it, headed on the quantifier; the *of* between the two nouns is the rectum's (rules 19, 31).
Rectum of the quantifying chain takes the *of* (rule 19).
Waw to *and*.
Noun.

review_notes: Corrected the `לַמֻּרְבָּכֶת` unit: the accepted alignment marked the assimilated article `unrepresented` under rule 29 and gave the whole *that which is soaked* to the participle under rule 46. But rule 46 governs an anarthrous substantive and directs the reader to let the presence of an article decide, and rule 41 gives a substantival article on a participle the supplied pronoun *that which*, headed on *that*, leaving the participle its own English with the supplied copula. The parallel `לַמַּחֲבַת` is untouched, because `מַחֲבַת` is a common noun and its article takes the ordinary *the* written before *pan*.

The verse's seven waws are matched one for one against the ASV's seven connectives (*also*, *and*, *whether*, *or*, *or*, *and*, *and*), so nothing is in surplus on either side and rule 14's correlative pair does not arise (rules 14, 42).
